nodes.label: 17-year-old male presents with 3 days of mouth pain and nonpainful penile erosions
One week prior, he experienced transient anosmia and ageusia that spontaneously resolved; he denied fever, cough, dyspnea, rhinorrhea, and gastrointestinal symptoms
He had taken acetaminophen and ibuprofen before presenting to the emergency department, but no medications before the onset of his mucocutaneous eruption

Physical examination showed he was afebrile with normal vital signs (respiratory rate 16 breaths per minute, oxygen saturation 97%); findings included shallow erosions of the vermilion lips and hard palate, circumferential erythematous erosions of the periurethral glans penis, and 5 small vesicles on the trunk and upper extremities, with the remainder of the examination unremarkable
COVID-19 (SARS-CoV-2) infection with associated mucocutaneous eruption
Erythema multiforme associated with viral infection
SARS-CoV-2 nasopharyngeal PCR was repeatedly positive
Testing for other respiratory pathogens and Mycoplasma pneumoniae IgM was negative
Mycoplasma pneumoniae IgG was elevated, indicating past infection rather than acute trigger
Skin biopsy with direct immunofluorescence has not yet been reported
HSV/VZV/enterovirus serology results are not yet available
Pathologist analysis concludes COVID-19-associated erythema multiforme is the most likely diagnosis based on current available data

Pathologist analysis states that final confirmation awaits skin biopsy/DIF and HSV/VZV/enterovirus serology, and that autoimmune bullous disease, HSV/Mycoplasma-related EM, and drug eruption are not fully excluded
Patient has Mycoplasma pneumoniae-associated erythema multiforme
